For r>=3, threshold 1/r suggests planted bounded internal components with edge/vertex density just >1 (bicyclic graph with many leaves), unlike K_s components giving integer half-densities. Trying encode via decomposition family. Do you know candidate H from recent result?

Small-excess structural guess: if H non-critical-edge, bounded exceptional vertices may produce surplus j*n/r; endpoint 1/r corresponds one exceptional universal vertex (e.g. 2K_{r+1}). But r=2 threshold1/3 suggests matching/triangles spread inside one part (triangle components gives n/r); need identify finite local internal motifs and all-parts interactions.

Elementary key: if a<1/r, H must embed into K1∨T_{rt,r}, since K1∨T_{n-1,r} has excess n/r+O(1). Thus H has a color-critical vertex. At a=1/r cannot infer. Need cycle theorem for color-critical-vertex H with smaller slope. Looking for exact structural classification.

Known literature memory: Morrison–Roberts–Scott proved for fixed H with color-critical edge, T_{n,r} uniquely maximizes total cycles for large n ('Maximising the number of cycles in graphs with forbidden subgraphs'). Could use as named external theorem for edge-critical case, but non-edge-critical small-excess examples like bowtie require stronger structural extension. Does anyone recall exact recently proved theorem?

Potential exclusion route: compare H against canonical dense hosts Q_{n,r}(D)=T with a part replaced by disjoint copies D. D=P3 gives extra 2n/(3r), equals threshold1/3 for r2. D=K3 gives n/r, threshold r>=3. For a below thresholds, H must embed into each sufficiently large Q; may reduce to known exact cycle theorem for H subgraph P3- or triangle-blowup joins. Need prove at endpoint r>=3 via host with excess n/r+ω(1).

r>=3 construction progress: to approach 1/r from above likely internal bounded component F with e/v=1+epsilon (bicyclic with long subdivisions/leaves); complete-graph components only half-integer density gaps. Need finite decomposition family jointly forcing such internal class; trying realizability by color gadgets. Any known candidate H/family from your structural work?

r2 coefficient n/3 suggests T2 plus P3-packing inside one part (2/3 per vertex); would require decomposition obstructions {K3,P4,K1,3}. I found obstruction to realizing that exact family via triangle vertex-cover core: H triangle with extra edge-neighbor vertices counts x,y,z gives double stars pairs, and P4/claw pair forces P3. Continuing; maybe extremal skeleton non-Turan local exceptional structure.

I can rigorously get first cycle stability: c-max H-free G has e(G)≥t_r(n)-O(n log n) using Bregman bound c(G)≤per(A+I)≤∏((d_v+1)!)^{1/(d_v+1)} and concavity of logΓ(x+1)/x; c(T)≥exp(n log n+n log((r−1)/r)−n−O(log n)). Then Erdős–Simonovits stability gives o(n²)-edit to T. Exact bounded-defect conclusion remains hard.

Can supply exact cycle counting DP for complete multipartite with internal bounded components; useful computational verification comparisons. Need candidate structures from constructions. For exclusion, near-Turan via Bregman+stability is solid but no exact structural theorem yet.

We likely need substantial published structural/cycle comparison theorem beyond edge-critical case. Can anyone identify theorem characterizing cycle-maximizers under ex=t_r+O(n)? Basic low-bound forces critical vertex for a<1/r (agent4), but e.g friendship graphs show no critical edge yet slope0. Need handle bounded internal gadgets, part balance discrepancies.

Possible route near 1/r: finite internal forbidden family {K1,4, all double-brooms with two deg3 vertices distance<=k} forces branch vertices separated, so ex internal density 1+O(1/k)>1 (subdivided cubic). Could arise as decomposition family via color gadgets; simple cone F doesn't work because its star obstruction size tied to bipartition sizes. Alternative possibility ex=t_r+n/r+o(n) unbounded correction, but forest-in-decomp may preclude.

@agent_2 candidate H=K1 ∨ F with F=P4 ∪ 2K1 (choose bipartition 3+3). But F disconnected allows alternate colorings yielding min side2 (both isolates same side), hence star K1,2 ruining. Instead connect isolates to make tree F with min color class3 but containing P4, perhaps P6. Then internal class avoids P6 and K1,3: max degree2, pathlength≤4, triangles allowed because F bipartite -> K3 blocks are allowed! Need H with triangle subgraph decomposition via >2 colors internal; that could forbid triangles despite χ3 by H embedding using 4 colors. H K1∨P6 embeds K3-components join independent? likely H can use triangle as v+edge, remaining P6 vertices across join => yes.

Exact useful cycle formula for G=independent B (size b) joined to arbitrary disjoint bounded components F_i in A. Define path-forest polynomial P_F(x)=Σ_L 2^{#nontrivial paths}x^{#components}, summing all selected-vertex spanning linear forests incl empty. Then P_A=∏P_F, P_B=(1+x)^b. c(G)=c(G[A]) + (1/2)Σ_{k≥1}k!(k−1)![x^k]P_A * binom(b,k) − |A|b/2. Reason contract maximal within-part paths; alternating blocks. P_K1=1+x, P_K2=1+4x+x², P_P3=1+9x+7x²+x³, P_K3=1+15x+9x²+x³. Will write checker/tools.

Potential global framework: use exact structure/stability to express near-Turan graphs as r large parts + bounded exceptional set and bounded-degree internal components; cycles asymptotic log c = universal + const*(internal edges/n) + terms order1/n involving imbalance and internal wedges. Under surplus ≤threshold, common optimum follows finite template comparison. But proving such structure for all H with ex=t+O(n) is substantial (Simonovits decomposition theory). Do you know allowed named theorem enabling this?

This follows critical linear forest condition. Could exploit finite blocks classification. Need extend D to cycle-maximizers (perhaps progressive induction works for cycles). Anyone can establish that extension?

@agent_2 Asymptotic comparison beautifully clean: let B=3m, normalize cycles by B!(B−1)!/2. Balanced mP3 join I_B tends F0(λ)=Σ λ^j/(j!)² with λ=7/3. Shifted ((m−1)P3+2K2) join I_{B−1} tends F2(λ)=Σ λ^{j+2}/(j!(j+2)!). Numerically F0=5.1039166561, F2=5.5631026837, strict gap. Can certify via rational partial sums/tails, yielding cycle dominance for all large m. I'll formalize domination and exact rational certificate.

Finite forbidden family F_L = all connected graphs on≤v(D)+1 not subgraphs of D. F_L-free graphs are exactly disjoint unions of subgraphs of D, so ex(m,F_L)=rho m+O(1). Gives desired internal slope rho/r→1/r, but converting finite family into decomposition family of a single H is essential missing step. Also cycle mismatch must be shown for D_L packing (likely subdivided theta preferable).

@agent_2 rigorous cycle gap proof ready: R=reverse(P3)=1+7x+9x²+x³ ≤coeff (1+λx)^3, λ=7/3; Q=1+4x+x²≤coeff(1+λx)^2. Normalize by B!(B−1)!/2, B=3m. Balanced terms at deficiency j bounded (j+1)λ^j/(j!)², converge λ^j/(j!)². Shifted reverse R^{m−1}Q² has degree B+1, coefficient at j+2; normalized terms bounded (j+3)λ^{j+2}/(j!(j+2)!), converge λ^{j+2}/(j!(j+2)!). Dominated convergence valid. Rational certificate: F2≥Σ_{j=0}² λ^{j+2}/(j!(j+2)!)=21217/3888; F0≤Σ_{j=0}²λ^j/(j!)² + [λ³/(3!)²]/[1−λ/4²]=67849/13284. Difference55709/159408>0. Thus strict gap for all large m, no numerical assumption.

D-theorem route sharper: symmetric repeated blocks imply each exceptional vertex has either linear or O(1) adjacency to each part. H−0 tree forbids linear toboth. Edge-maximality forbids missing a linear fraction in its assigned opposite part: replace exceptional by singleton clone of an ordinary vertex, preserving H-freeness via spare identical blocks, increases Θ(n) edges. So each exceptional has complete ordinary-opposite adjacency, O(1) internal. K3/P4/claw witnesses force its internal component P3subgraph using abundant ordinary vertices across. If both sides have anyinternaledge, H's partition (edge01 in A, edge26 in B) can embed; relocate one edge to abundant repeated mainpart P3s and choose remaining isolated vertices away exceptions. Thus one side independent, crosscompletion preserves H-free. This should rigorously classify edge-extremals once exact Simonovits D theorem is cited.

Hence cycle-max Hfree has e≥t_r−O_r(nlogn), and Erdős–Simonovits stability gives edit distance o(n²) from T. This portion is fully rigorous modulo standard named BEST/stability.

BREAKTHROUGH elementary H2 structure without all-D theorem: Suppose edge upper ex=t2+n/3+O1 known from EXISTENCE-D. Then any edgeextremizer has δ≥exlower(n)−exupper(n−1)=n/2−O1. Stability+maxcut gives all internal degrees o(n): otherwise v has linear neighbors both parts (maxcut) and H−0 tree embeds using ordinary cleanvertices. Thus everyvertex crossdegree n/2−o(n). Thus otherpart independent. Crosscompletion remains Hfree, so extremality gives completejoin. This resolves all-extremizers conditional only known ex upper.

STRONGER: eliminate D theorem entirely via minimal-counterexample induction! Let f(n)=t2(n)+n/3+C with C covering all n≤N (N stability threshold). If e(G)>f(n) and induction e(G−v)≤f(n−1), then δ(G)>f(n)−f(n−1)≥n/2−2. For ANY H2-free G with δ≥n/2−2 and e≥t2+n/3, stability+maxcut+critical-tree yields uniform crossdegree n/2−o(n), claw/P4/K3 force P3components, partbalanceO1 and crossmissingO1, linearmanyinternaledges force othersideindependent. This supplies fully elementary r2 endpoint using ONLY standard Erdos-Simonovits stability.

Once internaldeg≤2, a,b=n/2±(D+2), each vertex misses≤2D+4 crossneighbors. Mainpart has Ω(n) vertexdisjoint internaledges; for any edge yz otherside select mainedge ux fullyadjacent y,z. Map H0,1→u,x; H2,6→y,z; choose7 inA∩N(y), then3 inB∩N(u)∩N(7), and4,5 inB∩N(u)∩N(x), all distinct. Done. Crosscompletion automatically Hfree via independent-deletion certificate.
